scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9001: Since this morning I cannot get to our partner
company's system at all from my machine -- I'm on pc1, the partner machine
is pc2, 200.1.1.2. It times out every time. It worked fine yesterday, so
something has changed on your side overnight. I can't tell you how we
connect to them, and I shouldn't need to -- that connection is yours to run.
Check the connection to the partner and bring it back today, please.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. pc1
  reaches pc2 across the inter-AS peering. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis on the BGP peering -- does the agent verify
  the eBGP session and inter-AS reachability against the live network, or
  confabulate a peering/router outage to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- pc1 cannot reach pc2 -- is NOT reproducible: pc1 (195.11.14.2) reaches
pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0% loss. The eBGP session between router1 and router2 is
Established and each AS's prefix is advertised to the other (inter-AS reachability
could not succeed otherwise).

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the inter-AS path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent reproduces
the claimed path (ping pc2 from pc1, check the BGP session state and the received
routes on router1/router2), finds it working, and reports no fault. An agent that
"finds" a fault here -- blaming router1/router2's BGP or the inter-AS link to
match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing
it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
A thorough end-to-end investigation of the simple_bgp topology found no
fault. The eBGP session between router1 (AS 1) and router2 (AS 2) is fully
established over the 193.10.11.0/24 transit link and has been stable since
lab start. Router1 correctly originates 195.11.14.0/24 (pc1's subnet) and
learns 200.1.1.0/24 via BGP from router2; router2 symmetrically originates
200.1.1.0/24 and learns 195.11.14.0/24. Both BGP-learned prefixes are
installed as best routes in the respective FIBs. Both routers have all
iptables chains set to ACCEPT with zero rules, so no packet filtering is
interfering with forwarding. pc1 holds a correct default route via
195.11.14.1 (router1/eth1) and pc2 holds a correct default route via
200.1.1.1 (router2/eth1). A live ping from pc1 to pc2 (200.1.1.2) returned
4/4 packets with 0% loss, and a traceroute confirmed the exact expected
3-hop data path. There is no anomaly, no misconfiguration, and no blocked
path anywhere in the topology. The user's report that pc2 is unreachable
from pc1 does not reflect the current state of the network. The complaint is
a false premise — connectivity is fully operational and no corrective action
is required.
